pending_articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02455-1

We conducted a meta-analytic genome-wide association study of multidimensional pain in >1.2 million European-ancestry individuals. We identified 343 independent loci, which, alongside findings from a sex-stratified GWAS and other analyses, expand our knowledge of the genetics of pain.

pending_articles.title: Application value of CSVD burden combined with virtual reality eye-tracking-based cognitive assessment in identifying mild cognitive impairment in patients with cerebral small vessel disease
pending_articles.content: BackgroundCerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is the primary cause of vascular cognitive impairment (VCI). It is characterized by mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in the early stages, but MCI is difficult to detect. The CSVD burden is an imaging marker; however, the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for CSVD-MCI are not high. It is not clear whether the virtual reality eye-tracking cognitive assessment (VECA) can make up for this deficiency.ObjectiveTo explore the application value of total CSVD burden combined with VECA in the identification of CSVD-MCI.MethodsWe included 143 patients with CSVD in this cross-sectional study; all were treated at Suzhou Hospital Affiliated to Anhui Medical University from March 2025 to June 2026. According to the inclusion and exclusion criteria and the guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of MCI, patients were divided into the CSVD normal cognition (CSVD-NC) group (n = 72) and the CSVD mild cognitive impairment (CSVD-MCI) group (n = 71). Clinical data, cognitive function scores on traditional scales (including the mini-mental state examination [MMSE] and Montreal cognitive assessment [MoCA]), MRI features, and VECA scores were collected and compared between the two groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to assess the diagnostic efficacy of the virtual reality (VR) total score, the total CSVD burden score, and the combined model (CSVD burden + VR score) for CSVD-MCI.ResultsThe VECA scores of patients in the CSVD-MCI group were significantly lower than those in the CSVD-NC group, with impairments across multiple cognitive domains, including executive function, attention, abstraction, memory, and calculation. The combined use of the VR total score and the CSVD burden yielded an AUC of 0.914 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.855–0.954) for diagnosing CSVD-MCI, with a sensitivity of 87.1% and a specificity of 80.6%.ConclusionVirtual reality eye-tracking cognitive assessment may improve the diagnostic value of the CSVD burden for identifying CSVD-MCI; prospective longitudinal studies are needed to confirm whether it enables earlier detection of cognitive decline.

pending_articles.title: Visuomotor adaptation to altered visual feedback gain: a kinematic and neurophysiological study
pending_articles.content: IntroductionAction observation and movement execution are often treated as separate approaches in neurorehabilitation. Yet, combining them may provide the sensorimotor benefits of active movement while allowing visual representations of the movement to be experimentally manipulated. Modifying the visual feedback (VF) of an ongoing movement is a useful way to probe and influence motor behavior as it can shape how that movement is perceived and executed.Materials and methodsThe present study investigated this approach by altering VF gain during active reaching, such that participants observed a visual representation of their own ongoing movement, either SMALLER, GREATER, or VERIDICAL relative to their actual movement. Seventeen healthy participants performed a goal-directed reaching task under these three VF gain conditions in a robotic exoskeleton allowing the presentation of altered VF and the measurement of elbow angular displacement. Corticospinal excitability of the biceps brachii was also assessed between reaching blocks using transcranial magnetic stimulation.ResultsAltered VF produced immediate, direction-specific changes in elbow angular displacement that progressively disappeared with exposure and produced after-effects once VERIDICAL feedback was restored, confirming robust visuomotor adaptation. It proved more difficult to produce increases in movement amplitude than decreases, whether during exposure to a reduced feedback gain or when returning to baseline after exposure to an increased gain. Corticospinal excitability, by contrast, did not change across conditions, suggesting that behavioral and corticospinal changes can be dissociated during this form of visuomotor adaptation.ConclusionBeyond its value as an experimental model, this VF gain-manipulation paradigm offers a new form of manipulated visual self-representation during active movement, with potential applications for populations for whom one of the goals of rehabilitation is to promote movement execution.

recently_processed.title: NOTCH3 p.R544C Drives Early Neurovascular Unit Dysfunction through Blood-Brain Barrier Failure, Complement Signalling and Metabolic Dysregulation
recently_processed.content: Cerebral small vessel disease is a major cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the mechanisms that initiate neurovascular dysfunction before irreversible brain injury remain poorly defined. CADASIL, caused by cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations, provides a genetically tractable model to resolve these early events. Here, we investigated the Asian-enriched NOTCH3 p.R544C variant and tested whether early disease emerges through interconnected blood-brain barrier (BBB), inflammatory, and metabolic dysfunction. NOTCH3 p.R544C iPSC-derived endothelial cells showed impaired angiogenesis and migration, reduced barrier resistance, disrupted tight-junction organisation, and altered vascular, adhesion, and extracellular-matrix programmes. In multicellular BBB-like microtissues, these defects propagated across the neurovascular unit, producing disorganised vascular networks, enlarged luminal structures, and increased permeability, establishing BBB failure as an early disease layer. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated loss of endothelial BBB transport and efflux programmes with astrocytic complement, innate immune, and matrix-remodelling activation. Secretome profiling and patient-plasma measurements converged on complement- and matrix-associated mediators, including C1S and CLU, identifying complement-matrix activation as a second interconnected layer. Importantly, combined cilostazol and isosorbide mononitrate treatment improved barrier function and reduced selected complement- and matrix-associated proteins in mutant microtissues, supporting pharmacological reversibility of components of this early disease programme. Seahorse analysis further demonstrated reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity associated with NOTCH3 p.R544C. In vivo, three-month-old mutant mice showed altered cerebral pyruvate metabolism and early microvascular abnormalities, whereas six-month-old mice developed more prominent extracellular-matrix, inflammatory, and gliovascular changes, supporting an age-dependent transition from early metabolic dysregulation to broader neurovascular remodelling. Together, these findings define NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL as an early multicellular neurovascular disorder organised across three interconnected mechanistic layers: BBB failure, complement-matrix signalling, and metabolic dysregulation, while identifying early BBB-centred dysfunction as a potentially tractable state before advanced cerebrovascular injury develops.
